title: Completed extension-by-zero base change
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ satisfy [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and let
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
U'&\xrightarrow{g_U}&U\\
j'\downarrow&&\downarrow j\\
X'&\xrightarrow{g}&X
\end{array}
$$
be a cartesian open-immersion square [def-cbc-open-immersion-square]. Assume in addition that $j$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use the completed coefficient sheaves $A_T=\varprojlim_n(A/I^n)_T$ and $D(T_{\Proet},A)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Identify $A_X|_U=A_U$ and $A_{X'}|_{U'}=A_{U'}$ under the slice-site identifications [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Extension by zero $j_!$ and $j'_!$ means sheafification of the extension-by-zero module presheaf on these ringed slice sites [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], applied termwise to complexes. Let $K\in D(U_{\Proet},A)$ be derived $I$-complete [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. Then $j_!K$ is derived $I$-complete, and the canonical completed base-change map
$$
Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j'_!Lg_{U,\mathrm{comp}}^*K
$$
is an isomorphism, natural in $K$, where completed pullback is [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Both sides belong to the derived $I$-complete subcategory of $D(X'_{\Proet},A)$. The canonical map is the one induced by the finite-coefficient extension-by-zero base-change maps and the comparison between extension by zero and the derived limit of the strict reduction tower.

proof.text: For $e=j,j'$, slice restriction and sectionwise limits identify $A_T|_W=A_W$, preserving quotient projections. Base change makes $j'$ quasi-compact. Extension and restriction are exact, hence act termwise on derived categories.

proof.text: For a K-flat representative $P$, $\Delta P$ is K-flat on the diagram site: tensoring an acyclic system is acyclic at every level. Apply the strict ringed diagram tensor comparison to $\Delta C$ and $((P_n)_T)_n$, obtaining $(e_!C)_\bullet\cong e_!(C_\bullet)$, including transitions. Scalar restriction leaves the extension presheaf and its abelian sheafification unchanged.

source.place: Finite reduction and derived-limit assembly, with the quasi-compact-open correction.

proof.text: The ringed product lemma gives product preservation by $e_!$. Countable products are exact on both pro-etale module categories. The exact-product-functor theorem therefore gives the normalized natural isomorphism $\lambda_e:e_!R\lim M_\bullet\cong R\lim e_!M_\bullet$, preserving strict augmentations.

source.place: Finite reduction and derived-limit assembly, with the quasi-compact-open correction.

proof.text: Apply the tensor comparison to the finite free Koszul tower $Q_m$. Together with product preservation it identifies the completion fibers: $e_!F(C)=F(e_!C)$, since both differentials are $(dx,(1-s)x-dy)$. Both units are $(c\otimes1,0)$. Thus $e_!$ preserves intrinsic completeness. Apply this to $K$ and to the complete $Lg^*_{U,\mathrm{comp}}K$; completed pullback also makes the left endpoint complete.

source.place: Finite reduction and derived-limit assembly, with the quasi-compact-open correction.

proof.text: For the finite rings $P_n$, coefficient-compatible exchanges give an isomorphism of strict towers $g_n^*j_!K_n\cong j'_!g_{U,n}^*K_n$. The constant-to-completed finite comparisons identify these with the specified pullback towers, respecting every quotient transition; Step 2 identifies the input reduction tower.

source.place: Finite reduction and derived-limit assembly, with the quasi-compact-open correction.

proof.text: Apply functorial $R\lim$ to Step 5 and then $\lambda_{j'}^{-1}$. By definition this gives $Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K\cong j'_!Lg^*_{U,\mathrm{comp}}K$. All maps are natural. Presentation transport preserves finite exchanges and completion units; $\lambda$ preserves their strict augmentations. Hence the composite is the specified canonical comparison. Step 4 gives all completeness assertions.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NV-e9fdda156 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery against the live base (11 steps, 12891 chars), the human re-split note of 2026-10-21, the main-20261015 blueprint proof, and Stacks proetale 09BP (lemma-j-shriek-limits) and lemma-ses-associated-to-open. The item's statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to the base. The proof is now a 6-step assembly of 2012 chars, and the item is not on the route-pivot dropped list. The re-split note is answered: the one argument that had no node, the 09BP product kernel computation (old Step 4), is now the statement-only node lem-cbc-ringed-open-extension-products. The other long arguments are carried by statements of existing nodes: the diagram-site tensor clause of lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization, lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit, lem-cbc-finite-open-exchange-scalars and lem-cbc-adic-pullback-presentation-transport. Step 1: A_T|_W = A_W via slice localization and sectionwise limits; j' is quasi-compact by base change. Step 2: Tow_A(T) is the module category of the constant system on the vertical diagram site, where tensor and acyclicity are levelwise. So ΔP is K-flat, the reduction tower is ΔC ⊗^L (P_n), and the γ clause for arbitrary strict systems gives (e_!C)_• ≅ e_!(C_•) in D(Tow). Step 3: the new node plus exact countable products are exactly the hypotheses of the strict-limit node. Step 4: the slice tensor lemma applied to the finite free Koszul terms, together with product preservation and additivity, matches f_C, the fiber differential and the unit (c⊗1, 0). e_! is exact, so completeness is preserved, and the order of applications with completed-pullback-reduction is sound. Steps 5 and 6: finite exchanges as strict-tower inverse maps, then Rlim, then λ_{j'}^{-1}; this tower identification is the one NN accepted and is unchanged. The new node is true for any scheme X and any ring sheaf: SES kernel j_!F = ker(j_*F → i_*i^{-1}j_*F), and j_*, i_*, i^{-1} preserve products. Tested with U empty, U = X, the empty family and the zero ring. It strictly generalizes det-sf-open-closed-extension-zero-limits clause 3 (which needs X qcqs, while the item's X is arbitrary) and does not restate the item. Its B1-B7 points hold, and the three kinds of Mathlib search are recorded. There is no cycle and no SGA source. I accept the 12 declared tool_uses, including lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization as a generic ringed-diagram tool. Advisory only: the elementary flag on Step 4 is generous, and the presentation-transport citation in Step 6 is a leftover from the Lean history.
